domains.name: All assessment lenses
domains.question: Which evidence is reusable, and which decisions remain separate?
domains.scope: Separate assessment scopes; no single graph-wide compliance score.

domains.name: ESPR / DPP
domains.question: Can product identity, materials and lifecycle claims be traced?
domains.scope: ESPR DPP duties depend on applicable product measures and dates; a humanoid does not automatically require an ESPR DPP.

domains.name: Functional safety
domains.question: Does accepted evidence support this configuration in this task?
domains.scope: Functional safety is a discipline and assurance task. A single test result does not establish system safety.

domains.name: EU AI Act
domains.question: What is the AI function, intended use and applicable assurance route?
domains.scope: Classification, duty holder and sectoral route require assessment; a robot or AI assistant is not automatically high-risk.

domains.name: MDR · medical branch
domains.question: Would a medical intended purpose change the required evidence?
domains.scope: The base case is non-medical. A medical variant would require its own classification, clinical evidence and conformity route; these are not supplied here.

domains.name: Machinery Regulation
domains.question: Which risk assessment, technical documentation and conformity route apply?
domains.scope: Check the placing-on-market date and applicable machinery regime. The figure does not grant conformity or CE marking.

domains.name: Cyber Resilience Act
domains.question: Which software, vulnerabilities, support duties and incidents matter?
domains.scope: Determine product scope, exclusions and staged duties. An SBOM is useful evidence, not a complete CRA assurance case.

domains.name: Export controls
domains.question: What classification, destination, end user and end use must be checked?
domains.scope: No automatic licence requirement follows from the word robot. List entries, catch-all provisions and other relevant restrictions need case-specific review.
